roles.orchestrator: Every other module under src/, but tests.

role-paths.summary: The ESLint and dependency-cruiser configs give each module under src/ one role by its path, and verify checks that a file of each role has its role's rules.

unplaced-adapters.summary: no-restricted-syntax reports every module under src/adapters/ that is in neither driving/ nor driven/, which has no role.

depcruise-core-is-pure.summary: core-is-pure: a module under src/core/ imports nothing outside src/core/, including Node built-ins and libraries.

depcruise-orchestrators-import-no-adapte.summary: orchestrators-import-no-adapter: no orchestrator imports a module under src/adapters/.

depcruise-orchestrators-are-pure.summary: orchestrators-are-pure: no orchestrator imports a Node built-in.

depcruise-driving-adapters.summary: driving-adapters-import-no-driven-adapter: no module under src/adapters/driving/ imports one under src/adapters/driven/.

depcruise-driven-adapters.summary: driven-adapters-import-only-core-and-driven-adapters: a module under src/adapters/driven/ imports only the core and other driven adapters.

depcruise-entrypoint-is-not-imported.summary: entrypoint-is-not-imported: no module but a test imports src/main.ts.

depcruise-no-container.summary: no-container: no module imports a dependency-injection container: inversify, tsyringe, typedi, awilix and others.

depcruise-no-circular.summary: no-circular: no module depends on itself through others.

no-effects.summary: ESLint rule ts-baseline/no-effects, in the core and the orchestrators: no global that performs an effect (timers, crypto, fetch, storage, process, console, globalThis), no new Date() or Date.now(), no Math.random(), and no module-level let or var.

no-configuration.summary: ESLint rule ts-baseline/no-configuration, everywhere but src/main.ts and tests: no process.env, process.argv, import.meta.env or parseArgs.

max-lines-edges.summary: max-lines-per-function limits functions in src/adapters/ and src/main.ts to 50 lines.

complexity.summary: complexity is at most 10 everywhere: a warning, which check's --max-warnings 0 makes fail.

union-types.summary: A TypeScript union is closed: no other module can add a member, and the type checker rejects a value outside it.

banned-syntax.summary: no-restricted-syntax bans enums, default and optional parameters, and a class extending anything but JavaScript's own errors.

switch-exhaustiveness.summary: @typescript-eslint/switch-exhaustiveness-check: a switch on a union names every member, and has no default arm once it does, with considerDefaultExhaustiveForUnions and allowDefaultCaseForExhaustiveSwitch off.

no-unused-result.summary: ESLint rule ts-baseline/no-unused-result: no expression statement drops a Result.

no-unused-vars.summary: @typescript-eslint/no-unused-vars: no variable is assigned and never read.

prettier-check.summary: The shared check task runs prettier --check, and verify requires a project's check to run the shared one.

verify-prettier.summary: verify reports a Prettier option that differs from @ianflanagan1/ts-baseline/prettier.

dependency-units-keep-their-role.gap: A dependency's modules get no role of their own: the core may use no library at all, but an orchestrator may import any library, whatever role its module plays.

core-performs-no-effects.gap: A module-level const can hold a mutable object, browser globals such as window and document pass, and keeping state that changes across calls in an instance's fields (held-state) isn't detected.
proof: src/rulebook/conformance.test.ts: core-performs-no-effects misses a mutable const

core-libraries-are-pure.note: Stricter than the clause: the core may use no library at all.

orchestrator-performs-no-effects.gap: A module-level const can hold a mutable object, browser globals such as window and document pass, and keeping state that changes across calls in an instance's fields (held-state) isn't detected.

driving-adapter-imports-only-core-orches.gap: A port is declared in the orchestrator's module, which a driving adapter may import, so a driving adapter that takes a port isn't caught.

driving-adapter-calls-no-driven-adapter.gap: A driving adapter that declares an interface and is given a driven adapter through it by src/main.ts is not caught; only importing one is.

driven-adapter-calls-no-orchestrator.gap: A driven adapter that declares an interface and is given an orchestrator through it by src/main.ts is not caught; only importing one is.

wired-without-a-container.gap: Only the common container libraries are banned, not a service locator written in the project.

ports-declared-by-their-user.note: An orchestrator can't import an adapter, so it can't take an interface an adapter declares.

port-units-follow-typing.gap: A module of interfaces that other orchestrators import is an orchestrator like any other, so a ports module is not caught.

closed-families-are-sealed.gap: A family modelled as an interface that classes implement is not recognised as one, so any module can add a variant.

matches-on-closed-families-are-exhaustiv.note: Enums are banned, so a closed family is always a union. An if-else chain over one is not checked.

matches-on-closed-families-have-no-defau.note: TypeScript needs no catch-all: it knows a switch that names every member returns.

classes-extend-only-allowed-bases.note: JavaScript's own errors may be extended, so a thrown error can have a name of its own.

returned-failures-are-used.gap: A call that drops a sentinel, such as null, as a statement is not reported.
